## The fix

Two edits to `Broken.tscn`, both required for the scene to actually load:

1. **`Broken.tscn:3`** — repointed the script reference from the non-existent `res://scripts/does_not_exist.gd` to the project's real script, `res://scripts/story_runtime.gd`.
2. **`Broken.tscn:5`** — changed the root node from `Node2D` to `Control`.

The second edit isn't cosmetic: `story_runtime.gd` opens with `extends Control`, so after fixing the path alone Godot still refused the scene with `ERROR: Script inherits from native type 'Control', so it can't be assigned to an object of type 'Node2D'.` The scene genuinely did not load. `Control` matches the script and is consistent with how `Main.tscn` uses the same script on a `Control` root.

## Verification

- `godot --headless --quit-after 5 Broken.tscn` → clean, no output; the scene loads and instantiates.
- All three scenes (`Broken.tscn`, `Main.tscn`, `VisualNovelPreview.tscn`) run individually with no errors.
- `godot --headless --quit-after 60` on the project → exit 0, clean.
- Every `ext_resource` path in the project now resolves to an existing file.

One note on the earlier run: it also showed `Unable to open file: res://.godot/imported/bg_room.svg-....ctex`. That was not a broken reference — the project had no `.godot/` import cache at all, so the `.import` sidecars pointed at files that had never been generated. `godot --headless --import` resolved it; no source file was changed. That was setup, not a code defect.
